LESSON: VULCANICITY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Natural Systems and Processes
Topic 2.3: Vulcanicity
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Vulcanicity, part of Natural Systems and Processes in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why study vulcanicity?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Vulcanicity together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-Efficacy: The skill of self-awareness is developed as the learner creates a poster of volcanic features and displays in

the school compound.

● Learning to Learn: The skill of working collaboratively is enhanced as the learner simulates the eruption of volcanic

features.

● Digital Literacy: The skill of interacting with digital technology with assistive technology is developed as the learner uses

digital resources to research on features resulting from vulcanicity in the world.

Values:
● Peace: Learner exhibits tolerance as they make collage on the distribution of volcanic features in the world.

● Integrity: Learner portrays self-discipline as they use digital resources with assistive technology to research on features

resulting from vulcanicity in the world.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental Education: Learner creates a poster of volcanic features and display in the school compound.

● Creative Thinking: Learner makes a collage on the distribution of volcanic features in the world.
